title: Moqueca
subtitle: Brazilian coconut fish and prawn stew
excerpt: The great seafood stew of the Brazilian coast: firm white fish and prawns simmered in a fragrant broth of coconut milk, dendê (palm oil), tomatoes, and peppers. Bright, creamy, and subtly spiced, served with white rice and farofa.

recipe.sourceNotes: Moqueca is the signature seafood stew of the coastal Brazilian states, particularly Bahia and Espírito Santo, which have different but closely related versions. Moqueca baiana (from Bahia) uses dendê (red palm oil) and coconut milk, giving the stew its characteristic orange-red colour and rich, tropical flavour; this is the version with the deepest African culinary influence, brought by enslaved West Africans. Moqueca capixaba (from Espírito Santo) uses neither dendê nor coconut milk and is flavoured with annatto oil instead, producing a lighter, cleaner result. The version here is the Baiana style, the more widely known internationally. Dendê has a strong, distinctive flavour; a little goes a long way. Sunflower oil can be used if dendê is unavailable but the flavour will be different.

content.text: Marinate the fish briefly in lime and garlic before cooking; this seasons it through. Do not overcook the fish: it should be just set, not flaking apart. Add the prawns in the last 3 minutes. Dendê (red palm oil) has a strong flavour; start with 1 tablespoon and add more to taste.

content.text: Toss the fish with the lime juice, half the garlic, and a pinch of salt. Leave to marinate for 15 minutes. Heat the palm oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium heat. Layer the onion, peppers, tomatoes, and remaining garlic in the pan. Season lightly.
Lay the marinated fish chunks on top of the vegetables. Pour the coconut milk over. Add the chilli. Cover and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes without stirring.

Add the prawns, tucking them in around the fish. Cover and cook for a further 4 to 5 minutes until the prawns are pink and the fish is just set. Stir in half the coriander. Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt and lime. Scatter with remaining coriander. Serve with white rice.
